title: mitigate-admission-spillover-during-mixed-length-waves
creator: Riley Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated observed periodic throughput collapse and 95th/99th token latency spikes during high-variance traffic waves. Symptoms included small-request starvation, long-context requests dominating admission windows for multiple seconds, and transient KV cache churn. Scope: affects continuous batching scheduler across hosted pools and Dedicated GPU pools with mixed-length workloads. Private deployments reported related but rarer occurrences during rolling upgrades where admission state lingered. Goal: restore fairness for latency-sensitive short flows without regressing long-context throughput and avoid creating oscillations under bursty traffic.
comments: 2025-01-12 09:14 - Oncall (Eli Nguyen): Pager triggered for latencies >95th at 800ms for several hosted customers. Initial triage shows batcher admission windows filled by long-context requests for sustained 6-12s intervals.

2025-01-12 10:05 - Riley Patel: Escalated to Serving Runtime; created runbook and started correlation across tenant mix, model variants, and ingress patterns. Noted Dedicated pools show similar but more frequent symptoms under heterogenous tenant mixes.

2025-01-13 14:22 - Maya Rodriguez: Root cause hypothesis: admission window calculation uses rigid slot sizing that doesn't account for in-flight KV cache warming and per-tenant backlog shaping, allowing long-context waves to 'spill over' across multiple windows and starve small requests.

2025-01-14 11:40 - Maya Rodriguez: Proposed fixes: (A) add adaptive token-aware admission caps that reserve a soft percentage of admission capacity for short/latency-sensitive flows, (B) introduce a short-lived admission grace/jitter to break synchronization across hosts, (C) add a lightweight KV prefetch flag to prevent eviction storms when long requests arrive in waves.

2025-01-15 16:05 - Eng (Design Review): Chose incremental approach: implement (A) and (B) for immediate relief; implement (C) as opt-in follow-up for Dedicated/Private where KV sensitivity is higher. Added observability hooks to measure per-tenant admission share and token consumption over rolling windows.

2025-01-20 09:50 - PR opened (Maya): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289 implementing adaptive admission caps and admission jitter. Includes feature flag runtime.admission.soft_reserve_percent and runtime.admission.jitter_ms.

2025-01-22 13:30 - Code Review (Riley): Left feedback: ensure metric names are tagged by deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private) and add unit tests for edge cases where reserve_percent==0. Also request canary flag for private upgrades to avoid lingering state during rolling upgrade.

2025-01-24 08:12 - Maya Rodriguez: Addressed review comments; added metric tags and test coverage. Added migration step to clear admission hold states during Private upgrade window (edge-case observed in one customer report).

2025-01-25 22:10 - Oncall (Eli Nguyen): Canary rollout to 5% of Hosted fleet started with runtime-1.21.0 flags: soft_reserve_percent=18, jitter_ms=25. Early telemetry shows 30% reduction in 95th-token latency for short requests in canary hosts.

2025-01-27 17:45 - Observability (Sanjay Iyer): Dashboard updated: per-tenant admission share, token consumption histogram, kv-eviction-rate. Initial canary metrics: fair_share_metric improves from 0.62 to 0.87 for latency-sensitive tenants. No increase in overall cost per token observed in canary.

2025-01-29 10:03 - Customer Success (Ava Chen): Two Hosted customers confirmed perceived improvement in interactive latency during peak waves. One Dedicated customer reports improvement in throughput stability after enabling soft_reserve_percent via config toggle.

2025-01-31 15:00 - Performance (Maya): Extended canary to 30% and started Dedicated pool rollout to two low-risk clusters. Observed one Dedicated pool where admission jitter interacted poorly with existing autoscaler polity; disabled jitter there and collecting traces.

2025-02-02 12:22 - Incident Follow-up (Riley): For the Dedicated pool anomaly we identified autoscaler feedback loop: admission jitter increased short bursts causing scaler to overshoot. Mitigation: add autoscaler smoothing gate when admission-reserve toggles are active. Documented in follow-up task ENG-40477.

2025-02-03 09:10 - Maya Rodriguez: Next steps: complete rollout to remaining hosts after autoscaler smoothing gate deployed; enable KV prefetch opt-in for Dedicated clusters as configuration experiment; prepare RFC for long-term approach to admission that leverages ML-driven token forecasts. Due date: 2025-02-14.
2025-02-03 09:12 - Maya Rodriguez: Linked customer notes and support tickets: CS-7241, CS-7268. Closed loop with customers planned after full rollout.
notes: Risk: autoscaler interaction with jitter; Mitigation: gating and circuit-breaker. Success criteria: 50% reduction in 95th token latency regression alerts for latency-sensitive tenants and no regression in long-sequence tail throughput. Rollout plan includes staged canaries, Dedicated opt-in toggles, and a Private upgrade migration to clear admission state.
